title: Secrets on Campus
setting: Linden House, a converted Collegetown house at the top of the Buffalo Street hill in Ithaca, New York, run by Cornell as an overflow dorm. The night after a December snowstorm, finals week, present day.
briefing: Owen Castellano, the graduate resident advisor at Linden House, was found collapsed in the common-room doorway at twenty to midnight by Ray Kowalczyk, the night attendant, on his half-past-eleven round. The EMTs walked up from the pileup on the hill and pronounced him at ten past twelve: anaphylaxis. Owen had a severe tree-nut allergy the whole house knew about, and he had been eating from his own labelled, nut-free container of pesto. His EpiPen was not in his backpack, and the spare was gone from the kitchen first-aid cabinet. It looks like a terrible accident at the end of finals week, the kind of thing that happens to careful people exactly once. You are the campus police investigator who came up Buffalo Street on foot, because nothing with wheels is getting up that hill tonight. The county medical examiner and the crime-scene unit cannot reach Collegetown until the plows come through, and the front-door camera shows nobody came or went after Owen at half past nine. That leaves three people in the house, a pre-med senior, Owen's suite-mate and the night attendant, and they are yours until morning.

victim.name: Owen Castellano
victim.description: Graduate resident advisor, 26. Second-year PhD student in statistics and head TA for the intro statistics course half the pre-meds take. Careful, rule-bound, well liked. Severe tree-nut allergy; kept an EpiPen in the front pocket of his backpack and a spare in the kitchen first-aid cabinet, and told the whole house so at the September meeting.
victim.cause_of_death_public: Anaphylactic shock, the EMTs said, at about 23:35. Owen had a severe tree-nut allergy; his EpiPen was not in his bag and the spare was gone from the kitchen cabinet. He had been eating from his own labelled nut-free pesto. Until the medical examiner can get up the hill it is being treated as an accident.
victim.cause_of_death_truth: Anaphylaxis from finely ground walnuts stirred into his own labelled nut-free pesto at about ten past ten; both EpiPens in the house had been removed beforehand and thrown into the snow off the porch.

timeline_public.event: Owen comes in from the library, drops his backpack on the common-room couch, and says goodnight to Ray at the front desk.
Raised voices from Owen's suite on the second floor. Several residents hear it; nobody goes up.
Quiet hours. Hana says she went up to her room on the third floor to study.
Devin says he came down to the front desk to watch the late game with Ray.
The power flickers across Collegetown for about four minutes.
Owen comes down, heats his pesto in the kitchen microwave, and sits down to eat on the common-room couch.
Ray, on his half-past-eleven round, finds Owen in the common-room doorway, not breathing, and calls 911.
EMTs arrive on foot from the pileup on the hill. Owen is pronounced dead at 00:10.

timeline_truth.event: Owen comes in and drops his backpack on the common-room couch.

Owen and Devin argue in the suite about six hundred dollars missing from the house social fund. Owen says Devin is not the only one in the house he has given until Monday. On the back stairs, Hana hears 'Monday' and 'report'.

Hana, alone in the kitchen, grinds a handful of pantry walnuts in the house coffee grinder, stirs them into Owen's labelled nut-free pesto, rinses the grinder, and pushes the walnut bag back behind the flour.
Hana takes Owen's EpiPen from the front pocket of his backpack in the empty common room and the spare from the kitchen first-aid cabinet, and goes up to her room.
Devin comes down to the desk. Ray takes him to the basement laundry room, where nobody goes at that hour, to talk about the twenty-six hundred dollars.
Ray leaves Devin in the laundry room and comes up the back stairs. A page from his betting notebook falls out of his pocket onto the basement stairs.
Hana steps onto the porch and throws both EpiPens into the drift beside the steps. Ray, at the landing window, sees her and decides it was nothing.
Ray is back at the front desk.
Devin comes up, crosses the common room, and goes out onto the porch to phone his brother for money. He paces and smokes at the far rail until 23:25.
Hana carries her laundry, including the hoodie she wore in the kitchen, down the back stairs and starts the wash.
Hana moves the load to the dryer and goes back up to her room.
The power flickers. The dryer stops and does not restart.
Owen heats the pesto and eats it on the couch.
Devin comes in from the porch, passes Owen eating, and goes up to the suite with his earbuds in.
Owen's throat begins to close. He goes to his backpack: empty. He goes to the kitchen cabinet: empty.
Owen collapses in the common-room doorway.
Ray finds him on his round, calls 911, and starts CPR.
The EMTs pronounce him dead. The investigator arrives five minutes later.

locations.name: The Common Room
locations.description: Sagging couches, a TV, the house whiteboard by the door, and the side door onto the porch. Owen's backpack is on the couch where he always dropped it.

locations.name: The Kitchen
locations.description: A shared fridge with labelled shelves, a microwave, a coffee grinder on the counter, a first-aid cabinet by the door, and a pantry of things nobody remembers buying.

locations.name: The Back Stairwell
locations.description: Runs from the basement laundry room up to the third floor. The ground-floor landing has a window that looks straight down onto the porch steps.

locations.name: Owen's Suite
locations.description: Second floor. Two bedrooms off a small shared study; Devin has the second bedroom. Owen's desk is tidy: folders, a printer, and the house cash box on the shelf above it.

locations.name: The Laundry Room
locations.description: Basement. Two washers, two dryers, a folding table, a humming boiler. One dryer stands open, half-full and cold.

locations.name: The Side Porch
locations.description: Off the common room. Unshovelled snow on the boards; the steps lead down into a drift. It is still snowing lightly.

evidence.name: Owen's backpack
evidence.description: On the couch where he always dropped it. The front pocket is unzipped.
evidence.examined_detail: The front pocket is where Owen kept his EpiPen; the whole house knew, he made a speech about it in September. It is empty. The rest of the pocket, keys, a highlighter, a bike light, has been pushed to one side, as if someone felt for the pen without looking. Owen, who was tidy, would have zipped it. The spare he kept in the kitchen first-aid cabinet is gone too; Ray checked when the dispatcher asked.

evidence.name: The house whiteboard
evidence.description: By the door: the quiet-hours notice, a chore rota, fridge-shelf assignments.
evidence.examined_detail: Fridge shelves are assigned by netID in Owen's blocky capitals: TOP, oc311 (Owen), NUT-FREE, DO NOT TOUCH. 2nd, hs488 (Hana). 3rd, dm672 (Devin). Under the rota Owen has written MONDAY, boxed it, and underlined it twice.

evidence.name: Owen's pesto container
evidence.description: A glass container labelled OWEN, NUT FREE, DO NOT TOUCH, in the sink, scraped nearly clean.
evidence.examined_detail: Among the scrapings, fine pale grit that is not basil and not sunflower seed: ground walnut, milled almost to flour. On the drying rack the house coffee grinder has been rinsed but not dried, and there is walnut oil under the blade. In the pantry, the bag of shelled walnuts left over from the Thanksgiving bake has been pushed back behind the flour, half empty, with a green thumbprint on the twist-tie. Owen made this pesto himself with sunflower seeds; nobody else in the house touched it.

evidence.name: An academic-integrity report form
evidence.description: A printed form in the folder on Owen's desk, filled in by hand, unsigned.
evidence.examined_detail: Course: the intro statistics course Owen TA'd. Student: hs488, no name written. 'Final project substantially identical to a Fall 2023 submission (copy retained). Student informed Fri 12/12. Agreed to self-report to the academic integrity board by Mon 12/15, 9:00. If not, file.' The netID is the only identifier on the page.

evidence.name: The house social-fund cash box
evidence.description: A grey cash box on the shelf above Owen's desk, unlocked, with a ledger inside.
evidence.examined_detail: The ledger's last balance is $1,140. The box holds $540. A sticky note in Owen's hand on the lid: 'D. Monday. Last chance. O.' The shortfall is exactly six hundred dollars, and the withdrawals that don't add up start in October.

evidence.name: A page from a small notebook
evidence.description: A folded page on the basement stairs, near the bottom.
evidence.examined_detail: Block capitals in pencil: 'DM. BILLS +3.5. 400. TOTAL 2600. FRI.' Below it three more sets of initials with smaller numbers. The paper matches the pad on the front desk, and the handwriting matches the rounds log beside it.

evidence.name: Two EpiPens in the snow
evidence.description: Something orange in the drift beside the porch steps.
evidence.examined_detail: Two auto-injectors, safety caps on, unused: one loose, from Owen's backpack, and one still in the first-aid cabinet's box. They lie four feet out from the top step and a foot apart, thrown underhand from the porch, not dropped. Fresh snow has half-covered them; by morning they would have been gone until the thaw.

evidence.name: Footprints and cigarette butts on the porch
evidence.description: Tracks in the snow on the porch boards.
evidence.examined_detail: One set of big sneaker prints, pacing the far end of the porch, the rail end away from the steps, back and forth many times. Four cigarette butts stubbed out on the rail. Whoever stood here stayed a long while, faced the street, and never went near the steps.

evidence.name: A damp load in the cold dryer
evidence.description: Dryer 2 stands open and cold, half-full of wet clothes.
evidence.examined_detail: The power flicker at ten past eleven stopped it and nobody restarted it. On top of the load: a maroon pre-med society hoodie with SATO-REYES across the back. The wash did not get everything. There is a green smear inside the right cuff, and in the seam of the cuff, fine pale grit. Pesto, and ground walnut.

dynamic_evidence.name: The dryer's lint trap
dynamic_evidence.description: Dryer 2 is running again, hot. The lint trap has been pulled out and pushed back crooked.
dynamic_evidence.examined_detail: A fresh mat of maroon fluff in the trap, and caught in it a fleck of green and a few pale grains that crumble like nut. Somebody restarted the dryer in a hurry; the hoodie inside is bone dry now, but the lint kept what the cuff was carrying.

suspects.name: Hana Sato-Reyes
suspects.public_description: Biology major, pre-med, three months from graduating. Lives on the third floor. Says she was in her room with headphones on going through flashcards from ten o'clock until she heard Ray shouting for help.
suspects.persona: Twenty-one, composed, precise, exhausted: the kind of student who has never failed at anything and built her whole life on that. On Friday Owen told her he had found her final project was copied and gave her until Monday to self-report; a finding would void her medical-school acceptance. She decided on Saturday afternoon. She has told herself it was the only way and mostly believes it. She is not sorry yet. She is terrified.
suspects.speech_quirk: Answers like a med-school interview: composed, complete sentences, and she thanks the detective for the question ('That's a fair question'). Says 'to be honest' right before a lie. When rattled she numbers things ('Two things. One,') to stay in control. Calls Owen 'Owen', never 'the victim', and uses clinical words for feelings ('I'm just depleted').
suspects.portrait_prompt: College senior, early twenties, olive skin, long dark hair pulled back in a ponytail, thin wire spectacles, grey sweatshirt, tired composed face, pixel-art portrait, dorm lamplight
goals: Get through tonight without anyone connecting her to Owen's course.
Keep the detective looking at Devin: the argument about Monday was real, and it was about him too.
Get back down to the laundry room before anyone else does.
knowledge: Owen was the head TA for the intro statistics course. On Friday afternoon he told her he had found that her final project was substantially identical to a submission from two years ago, a file from a folder of old projects that gets passed around the pre-med group chat. He gave her until Monday at nine to self-report to the academic integrity board or he would file the report himself. A finding would void her conditional acceptance to medical school.

At about five past ten tonight, with the common room empty, she ground a handful of walnuts from the pantry bag in the house coffee grinder, stirred them into Owen's labelled nut-free pesto, rinsed the grinder, and pushed the walnut bag back behind the flour. Then she took Owen's EpiPen from the front pocket of his backpack on the couch and the spare from the kitchen first-aid cabinet.
At about twenty-five to eleven she stepped onto the porch and threw both EpiPens into the drift beside the steps, hard, so the snow would cover them by morning. She saw no one.

At about quarter to eleven she took her clothes, including the maroon pre-med society hoodie she had worn in the kitchen, down the back stairs to the basement and ran them through the wash, then the dryer. She does not know that the power flicker at ten past eleven stopped the dryer.
At quarter to ten she was on the back stairs and heard Owen and Devin shouting in the suite. Owen said 'Monday' and 'I'll have to report it'. Devin has been broke since October.
Ray, the night attendant, is normally at the front desk all night and does his rounds on the half hour. She has never seen him anywhere else in the house.
Owen's tree-nut allergy, and where he kept both EpiPens: he told the whole house at the September meeting.
The pesto was Owen's weekly batch. He made it with sunflower seeds instead of pine nuts, labelled it, and nobody else in the house ever touched it.

secrets.text: She was not in her room from ten o'clock until the sirens. She went down to the kitchen at about ten, and down to the laundry room at about quarter to eleven.
secrets.cover_story: She was in her room on the third floor with her headphones on, going through flashcards, from ten o'clock until she heard Ray shouting for help. She never came down.

suspects.name: Devin Marsh
suspects.public_description: Economics senior and Owen's suite-mate on the second floor. Known around the house for his sports bets. Says he was down at the front desk with Ray watching the late game from about quarter past ten until Ray went on his round.
suspects.persona: Twenty-two, charming, restless, and in a hole: a sports-betting habit that turned into a twenty-six-hundred-dollar debt to the night attendant and six hundred dollars 'borrowed' from the house fund. Owen was the closest thing he had to a brother in Ithaca and he was still lying to him. He did not kill Owen. He looks exactly like someone who did.
suspects.speech_quirk: Fast and jokey; calls the detective 'boss'. Starts a sentence with 'Look,' when he is about to lie. Uses betting talk ('I'd put money on it', 'that's not the play', 'long odds'). When scared the jokes get worse, not fewer.
suspects.portrait_prompt: College senior, early twenties, fair skin, short blonde hair under a backwards cap, stubble beard, grey sweatshirt, restless grin, pixel-art portrait, dorm lamplight
goals: Not be the guy they pin this on; he knows how it looks.
Keep Ray out of it. Ray fronted him when nobody else would, and Ray loses his job if the book comes out.
Keep the six hundred dollars quiet until he can put it back.
knowledge: He took six hundred dollars from the house social-fund cash box in October to cover a bet, meaning to put it back. Owen found the shortfall on Friday and, in the argument at quarter to ten tonight, gave him until Monday to replace it or he would report it to Residential Life.
During that argument Owen said: 'You're not the only one in this house I've given till Monday, and the other one has a lot more to lose than six hundred dollars.' Owen would not say who.
He owes Ray Kowalczyk, the night attendant, twenty-six hundred dollars from bets Ray placed for him. Ray took him down to the laundry room at about quarter past ten and told him it was due by Friday.

From about twenty to eleven until nearly half past eleven he was on the porch, pacing and smoking at the far rail, on the phone with his brother in Buffalo asking for money. His brother said no. It was dark and snowing and he never looked at the steps or the drift.

At about twenty-five past eleven he came in through the porch door and passed Owen on the couch eating his pesto out of the container. Owen did not look up and they did not speak. Devin went up to the suite with his earbuds in.

Owen's tree-nut allergy: the whole house knew. Owen kept an EpiPen in the front pocket of his backpack and a spare in the kitchen first-aid cabinet, and made a speech about both at the September house meeting.
Hana Sato-Reyes is the only pre-med in the house. She has been strange all week, up at all hours, and she bit his head off on Thursday for using her fridge shelf.

secrets.cover_story: He was down at the front desk with Ray from about quarter past ten, watching the late game on Ray's phone, until Ray went on his round and started shouting.

suspects.name: Ray Kowalczyk
suspects.public_description: Night attendant for the university's Collegetown houses, nineteen years. Says he was at the front desk all night apart from his rounds on the half hour, with Devin keeping him company from quarter past ten, and found Owen on the eleven-thirty round.
suspects.persona: Fifty-four, nineteen years on nights in the Collegetown houses, two years from a pension. Big, slow, watchful; a townie who likes the kids more than he lets on. Takes bets on the side because the pay is what it is. He saw something tonight that he has decided was nothing, because if it was not nothing he will have to explain where he was standing and why.
suspects.speech_quirk: Slow, few words; calls the detective 'officer' whatever the rank and the residents 'the kids'. Answers 'Yep' or 'Nope' first and then one sentence. Says 'I been here nineteen years' whenever his competence is questioned. Never swears.
suspects.portrait_prompt: Night security attendant, mid-fifties, brown skin, close-cropped grey hair, grey moustache, reading spectacles on a cord, navy uniform jacket with a badge, heavy-set, pixel-art portrait, lamplight
goals: Keep his job: nineteen years in, two to pension.
Keep the betting quiet; it is a firing offence and probably worse.
Do right by Owen, who was a good kid, without saying the one thing that costs him his job.
knowledge: He has worked nights in the Collegetown houses for nineteen years. He takes sports bets for a handful of students because the pay is what it is. Devin Marsh owes him twenty-six hundred dollars.

At about quarter past ten he took Devin down to the laundry room, where nobody goes at that hour, and told him the money was due Friday or he would take it up with the university. That was a bluff; he would lose his job before Devin lost anything.

Coming up the back stairs at about twenty-five to eleven he stopped at the landing window and saw Hana Sato-Reyes at the top of the porch steps throw something small into the drift, twice, underhand, then go back inside. He thought: a vape, whatever, kids. He was back at the desk by twenty to eleven.

On his half-past-eleven round he found Owen in the common-room doorway, face swollen, not breathing, the backpack open on the couch. He called 911 at 11:38 and started CPR. When the dispatcher asked, he checked the kitchen first-aid cabinet for the spare EpiPen: it was gone.
The front-door camera feeds the monitor on his desk. Nobody came in or went out of the front door after Owen at half past nine. The porch door has no camera.
Owen was the best RA he has had in the building: strict about rules, decent about people. A week ago Owen told him 'somebody in this house is going to have a bad Monday' and would not say more.
Devin went out to the porch at about twenty to eleven and stayed out there until nearly half past; Ray could smell the smoke from the desk every time the porch door opened.

solution.method: Finely ground pantry walnuts stirred into Owen's own labelled nut-free pesto at about ten past ten; both EpiPens in the house removed beforehand and thrown into the snow off the porch so that the reaction could not be stopped.
solution.motive: Owen, as head TA, had found that Hana's final project for the intro statistics course was copied from a previous year's submission and had given her until Monday morning to self-report to the academic integrity board or he would file the report himself. A finding would have voided her conditional acceptance to medical school.

red_herrings: Devin lied about being at the front desk and has a documented six-hundred-dollar problem with the victim. 'D. Monday. Last chance.' reads like a motive; it is a deadline about the house fund, and Owen gave the same deadline to someone with far more to lose.
Ray, the one adult in the building, is lying about where he was. He is covering a betting book, not a murder, and his lie is what kept him from saying what he saw.
Devin and Ray alibi each other. It looks like collusion in a killing; it is collusion over a gambling debt.
Devin's footprints and cigarette butts put him on the porch for most of an hour, four feet from where the EpiPens landed. He never saw them.

rumor_seeds.text: Devin and Owen were shouting about money and 'Monday' in the suite at quarter to ten. Whatever Devin says about the front desk, he has been broke since October.
If they ask, we were at the desk the whole time. I'm not bringing up the laundry room and neither are you.

ticker_lines: A phone buzzes somewhere upstairs and is silenced at once.
The plow goes by on the hill without stopping.
Someone runs water in the kitchen, briefly.
The porch door sticks, then bangs shut.
Two of them pass on the back stairs without a word.
